newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAMANCOR SEES ALLOY PRICES UP, FLAT H2.
newsitem.headline: SAMANCOR SEES ALLOY PRICES UP, FLAT H2.

text.p: JOHANNESBURG, Feb 10 (Reuter)3 - South African ferro-alloy producer Samancor said on Monday an expected rise in world chrome and manganese prices by mid-1997 should boost earnings for these sectors in the second half of the year.

However Samancor's executive chairman Mike Salamon said this meant no major recovery for the company from huge loses it suffered due to low prices on the international alloy markets and low throughput from its Columbus Stainless joint-venture in 1996.
He said Columbus -- one of the world's biggest stainless steel producers -- would post a clipped performance in 1997 due to extended commissioning problems.
Columbus is a joint venture between Samancor, the state's Industrial Development Corporation and Highveld Steel and Vanadium Ltd .
"Some upward alloy price movement can be expected by mid-1997," he told a results presentation conference.
"However, higher interest costs and the termination of capitalisation of interest and costs at Columbus will act to negate this improvement," he added.
Samancor earlier reported earnings per share of 90 cents compared to 201 cents in the previous period for the six months ending December 1996.
It declared a a dividend of 30 cents per share, down from 60 cents for the same period in 1995.

Salamon said commissioning problems at Columbus as well as low stainless steel prices had contributed to the loss of 14.6 million rand at the unit in the past six months compared to a profit of 10.0 million rand from Columbus in the same period.
Samancor's attributable income for the six months to end-December plunged to 171.43 million rand from 381.92 million attained in the same period in 1995.
Analysts last week had predicted a dismal perfomance by Samancor for the first half of this year, saying the 1996 ferro-alloys market had been depressed.
They said Samancor should expect to post better results next year when the world's steel production is expected to rise by about two percent.
